## ✨ Highlights

- 🛰️ **A cluster member's page tells its BGP state**: when the cluster manages BGP, the member's top bar says what the node announces - **BGP announcing**, **BGP withdrawn** (its routes held down: HAProxy not answering, or the member drained) or **BGP down** (no session) -, as it already gave the member's VRRP role. And when the Controller can read the router in front, the router's choice next to it: **multipath**, **master**, **backup** or **absent** ([clusters](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md)).

## 🧩 Clusters

- **The member's BGP state on its page** ([#354](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/354)): read from the node itself, always there - whether the router uses the route is the router's to say, and the node can't know it. The tooltip lists each BGP session.
- **A read-only RouterOS hook** ([#354](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/354)): for a cluster whose members announce the service addresses over BGP, the RouterOS balancer hook gets a **Read only** option (the cluster's **Balancer in front** card, `read_only` in the API and in Terraform's `janus_cluster`, `janusctl cluster balancer -read-only yes`). It writes no route - it removes those it wrote before, a static route would beat BGP's - and reads the router's routes to each prefix: each member's role shows on the card (**Router says**) and on the member's page, IPv6 routes included (their next hop is the member's link-local address). The router user needs only `read,api,rest-api`. A router the Controller can't reach: the pages show the node's side alone, the card says why.
- `GET /api/clusters/{id}/router`: the router as the hook reads it, at most every 10 s per cluster.

## 🧪 Tests

- A fake RouterOS router with IPv4 and IPv6 routes: the read-only hook removes its former route and leaves BGP's alone, each member's role per prefix (a link-local gateway included), the member page served from the reading's cache, a drain writes nothing; `read_only` refused with `distance`, `check_gateway` or on a webhook.
- Proven on the lab: two members announcing the same anycast address to a RouterOS 7.25 router, read by a read-only hook - both multipath, one drained (master / withdrawn and absent), the router on a single path (master / backup), a session cut (down and absent), the router unreachable (the node's side alone).
